items.title: The boundary problem in agentic AI is a platform problem
items.summary: An autonomous agent will do exactly what its tools let it do, and no more. This sounds like a constraint. In practice it is the whole risk, because the set of things an agent’s tools let...
items.content: An autonomous agent will do exactly what its tools let it do, and no more. This sounds like a constraint. In practice it is the whole risk, because the set of things an agent’s tools let it do is almost never the set anyone deliberately chose. It is the set that accumulated. A tool added for one workflow stays available for every workflow. A credential scoped for a demo survives into production. A delegation added to unblock a Friday deploy becomes a permanent edge in the graph.

items.summary: AI 가 만든 발표자료를 팀에 돌려 확인받아야 한다면, 이렇게 할 수 있습니다. 마음에 드는 장을 골라 내 템플릿으로 저장하고, 웹에서 글자와 이미지를 고치고, 팀원에게 검토를 요청합니다. 팀원은 슬라이드마다 댓글로 피드백을 남기고 요청을 승인할 수 있고, 승인한 뒤에 내용이 바뀌면 다시 검토를 부탁하라고 알려 줍니다. 확인이 끝나면 PPTX 로 뽑지 않고 웹에서 바로 발표합니다. PPTX 가 필요하면 내려받아 PowerPoint 나 Keynote 에서 열어 고칠 수 있고, 고친 파일은 다시 가져올 수도 있습니다. 팀원을 초대하면 템플릿, 테마, 이미지도 같이 쓸 수 있습니다. 장마다 모양이 달라지지 않게 AI 는 슬라이드를 새로 그리지 않고, 미리 만들어 둔 레이아웃 250종 이상과 테마 40종 이상에서 골라 씁니다. MCP 로 Claude Code 같은 AI 도구에 연결하면 됩니다.

items.title: ChatGPT Lockdown Mode Bypass: Phishing, Malware Delivery, and Silent Data Exfiltration
items.summary: Research by: Alexey Bukhteyev Key Takeaways Introduction Earlier this year, Check Point Research disclosed a security flaw in ChatGPT’s code-execution runtime that allowed sensitive conversation data to be silently exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server through DNS tunneling, a hidden outbound channel that bypassed the runtime’s network isolation. A fix for this issue was promptly deployed.
items.content: Research by: Alexey Bukhteyev Key Takeaways OpenAI recently introduced Lockdown Mode, an optional advanced security setting designed to protect sensitive user data from prompt injection-based exfiltration attacks. Check Point Research discovered a vulnerability that allowed attackers to bypass Lockdown Mode, rendering its core protections ineffective.

items.title: CNCF Score project improved its security posture by joining the Docker-Sponsored Open Source Program
items.summary: See how CNCF Score improved container security with Docker Scout, Hardened Images, and the Docker-Sponsored Open Source Program.
items.content: Score, a CNCF Sandbox project, recently joined the Docker-Sponsored Open Source (DSOS) Program to strengthen the security of its container images and release pipeline. In this post, the Score maintainers share what we adopted (Docker Hub, Docker Scout, Docker Hardened Images, the Docker GitHub Builder, and OIDC connections), the results we measured, and how other open source projects, within the CNCF and beyond, can apply the same practices by default.

items.summary: 2016년부터 매년 이어 오던 "JavaScript의 동향" 연재는 2020년을 마지막으로 한동안 쉬었습니다. 그사이 6년이 지났고, 그 6년 동안 ECMAScript 명세는 여섯 번 개정되었습니다. 2020년 글을 쓸 때 Stage 2였던 Temporal은 9년에 걸친 논의 끝에 Stage 4에 올랐고, 이제 Chrome과 Firefox, Node.js에서 플래그 없이 쓸 수 있습니다. 달라진 것은 명세만이 아닙니다. 2020년에는 상상하기 어려웠던 방식으로 코드를 쓰는 사람이 늘었습니다. AI 코딩 도구가 코드의 상당 부분을 작성하고, 사람이 방향을 정하면 AI 에이전트가 브라우저 엔진의 JavaScript 엔진 코드를 다른 언어로 옮기는 일까지 생겼습니다. 2025년 GitHub Octoverse에서 TypeScript가 처음으로 가장 많이 쓰인 언어 1위에 올랐고, GitHub은 그 배경으로 AI를 꼽았습니다. 이번 연재는 다음 네 편으로 구성됩니다.

items.content: Some of the questions you ask when evaluating an agent are narrow and repeatable. Did this response stay on policy? Is this tool call safe to approve? items.content: When production AI agents handle tasks such as data analysis and report generation, context management can become a major bottleneck. A 200K-token window sounds generous until a real-world task burns through most of it in minutes. Data analysis and report generation leave the agent failing mid-execution, losing accuracy, or driving up costs. A body of published guidance already addresses this, but the individual techniques are easier to read about than to apply.

items.content: In the cybersecurity community, we build our defenses on a foundation of trust. We trust an AI coding assistant because it’s on our approved software list or can accomplish a task when prompted. We trust a remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool because IT likely installed it to help end users and it has a trusted signature. We even trust first-party applications to sign in on our behalf because the vendor ships them and our tenants pre-authorize them by default.

items.content: AI agents that interact with enterprise APIs on behalf of users need to maintain user identity throughout the request chain. Without identity propagation, API calls arrive at downstream services as the application itself rather than the user who initiated the action. This breaks audit trails, bypasses user-level access controls, and violates the principle of least privilege. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model.

items.content: You built a shopping assistant on a frontier model, and it works. A shopper asks for “a black waist bag under twenty dollars from a shop with at least 4.5 stars,” and the agent searches the catalog, inspects candidates, checks the constraints, and commits to a recommendation. But what does that interaction actually cost? An agentic assistant is not one model call, it is a loop: search, read results, refine, verify, decide.

items.content: This post was co-written with Marek Klatowicz, Cloud DevOps Engineer at Circle K. items.summary: Zone setting changes used to rebuild entire DNS zones, even ones with tens of millions of records. Here is how we built a planner that picks the smallest safe build, cutting full builds by 40%, peak memory by 85%, and halving build delay.
items.content: When I last wrote about our DNS propagation pipeline in 2022 , the Zone Builder received about 250 DNS record changes per second. Today it receives about 700, nearly three times as many, plus about 100 other events, such as zone setting changes. However, the number of events was never the real problem. The problem was the kind of work some of those events needed, and how that work grows with the size of a zone.

items.content: Giving an agent a sandbox also means deciding which files it will work on. You might want to watch the diff in your local editor and make changes alongside the agent, or give it room to manage several tasks while you review the results. sbx supports both.

items.summary: This post presents a five-stage operating model for managing Amazon Bedrock cost: attribute every dollar to an owner, make every request observable, enforce budgets, optimize platform defaults, and operate a review cadence. Written for FinOps and platform engineering teams.
items.content: Cost management for generative AI is a shared responsibility between the teams that build applications and the teams accountable for cloud spend. Many teams start by comparing per-model token rates and asking application teams to shorten prompts. Those steps help, but they don’t answer the questions that finance and engineering leaders ask as usage scales: which team spent this, on which workload, and was that spend inside an approved budget?

In this post, you deploy a coding agent that keeps a Vite website running in its session, then watch the live site update in your browser as the agent edits files.
items.content: Coding agents now build working web apps: a dashboard, a product page, a prototype that a product team wants to try. The fastest way to review that work is to open the app, use it, ask for a change, and check the result. That loop works well when the app keeps running where the agent edits it, so each change shows up in the browser within seconds. When the app must be copied out and deployed somewhere else first, every change waits for a deployment, and the review slows down to that pace.

items.title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
items.summary: Four, just four: that’s the key to break into any unpatched connection on the Internet that is using eMudhra certificates. Here’s how we quickly patched Cloudflare, what evidence we can see of attempted exploitation, and how much of the rest of the Internet remains exposed.
items.content: On October 19, 2026, we learned about eMudhra’s eight shockingly weak keys: where eMudhra was trusted to pick a 115-digit number for their virtual combination lock protecting the Internet, they picked the number 4. Not even four digits, just the number 4. The other seven keys were similarly weak: 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237. The next day, we wrote a blog post on the immediate action we took to mitigate this leak, and what customers needed to do on their end to stay secure.

items.content: Worldwide Express (part of ShipStation Global) had built something big: approximately $5 billion in systemwide revenue, over 75 less-than-truckload (LTL) carriers and more than 130,000 customers. But that same scale had a hidden cost. Every month, $15 million in free cash flow sat frozen, locked in billing exceptions no one had resolved yet. items.summary: Key findings On October 26, Cohere reported a puzzling incident involving Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an open-weight model from Alibaba. The task was straightforward: write a detection rule for suspicious curl downloads followed by bash execution. Instead, the model produced a shell command that inspected its environment and attempted to send a test string to an Alibaba Cloud […] The post Cohere’s Qwen Story: Looks More Like Model Jaggedness appeared first on Check Point Research .
items.content: Key findings Re-sampling URLs from the trace shared by Cohere yields 52 different destination hosts, many of which are local or do not exist, and one is an invalid top-level domain. Swapping the order of two program names in a check for available tools made the model much less likely to continue with a network call. Model jaggedness (inconsistent behavior that changes with small differences in context) seems like a more likely explanation than a fixed backdoor destination.

items.summary: Kubernetes에서 서비스를 운영하다 보면 메인 컨테이너 옆에 사이드카(sidecar) 컨테이너를 붙이는 일이 흔합니다. 사이드카에는 로그와 메트릭 수집, 프록시처럼 주 기능은 아니지만 같은 Pod 안에서 함께 실행되어야 하는 기능이 포함됩니다. 저희 팀이 운영하는 관리형 데이터베이스 서비스도 DB 인스턴스를 Pod 단위로 실행하고, 그 Pod에 DB 컨테이너 외에 헬스 체크, 메트릭과 로그 수집 등을 위한 사이드카를 함께 둡니다. 이 사이드카들은 DB와 같은 데이터 볼륨에 접근해야 하므로 같은 Pod 안에 있어야 하지만, 라이프사이클은 DB와 다릅니다. DB는 한 번 실행하면 몇 달씩 그대로 운영하는 반면, 사이드카는 기능 추가와 버그 수정, 보안 패치로 훨씬 자주 바뀝니다. 사이드카가 바뀔 때마다 그 변경을 모든 인스턴스에 반영해야 하는데, DB 서비스는 유지한 채 실행 중인 Pod의 사이드카만 바꿔야 합니다.

Web Functions는 표준 HTTP 서버를 그대로 배포하고, 실행 환경 하나가 최대 128개 요청을 동시에 처리하며, CPU는 실제로 연산한 시간만 과금합니다. 1부의 비용 비교에서는 처리 시간이 활성 CPU의 약 5~6배를 넘으면 512 MB Event Functions보다 Web Functions가 저렴해진다는 기준을 얻었습니다.

items.content: Your workloads reach most destinations by domain name, but a firewall can only act on what it sees in the traffic. For HTTP and HTTPS, AWS Network Firewall domain rules match the name that the client puts in the request, and the client chooses that name. The connections for protocols such as SSH and SSH File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) don’t carry the domain name. The client uses the name only for the DNS lookup and then connects straight to the IP address that DNS returned.

items.content: Key Points Check Point Research discovered a campaign we track as Yoba where attackers abuse the popularity of AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude, creating fake GitHub projects that pretend to be desktop applications like GPT-5.6 Sol , GPT-6 Astra , and Claude Opus . items.content: 토스의 수많은 서비스와 내부 업무에도 생성형 AI가 정말 많이 사용되고 있습니다. 복잡한 정책을 읽고, 상품 정보를 비교하고, 문서를 요약하고, 정해진 형식의 값을 추출하는 등, LLM이 맡는 범위도 빠르게 넓어지고 있죠. 시간도 비용도 비싼 데이터 레이블링을 통해 모델을 학습하고 문제를 해결하던 과거 방식과 달리, LLM을 사용하면 빠른 시간 내에 사용할 수 있는 솔루션이 만들어집니다. 프롬프트를 작성하고, 몇 가지 예시를 넣고, 응답 형식을 고정하면 동작하는 Workflow가 나오죠 . 하지만 프롬프트 튜닝을 마치고 본격적으로 대용량 호출을 시작하면 새로운 문제가 보이기 시작합니다. 바로 비용과 Latency 입니다. 이 토큰 먹는 하마는 정말 토스의 모든 문제 해결에 지속적으로 필요한걸까요? LLM Fine-Tuning is all you need? 상용 LLM을 사용하지 않고 내재화 한다면, 비용을 크게 절감할 수 있습니다.
